## Summary

Two failures from one production incident, both in the path a silo takes as it starts. A slow sibling silo crash-looped both kernel replicas, and the projection registrations that timed out against them never recovered — leaving a consuming application's read model frozen for a day while every layer reported success.

## Fixed

- A silo no longer terminates when a grain call made during startup cannot reach a sibling silo that has not stabilized yet. The failures a forming cluster produces are now retried wherever they occur in the startup task, rather than at whichever individual call site was last discovered to be unprotected. A step that still fails once the retry budget is spent fails the host as before, so a genuine defect is not started around (#4051)
- A projection can no longer stay permanently unsubscribed. The activation-time resubscribe no longer holds the projections manager's turn while it runs, so registrations arriving during it are answered instead of timing out; and a registration now reconciles projections that are registered but not subscribed, instead of deciding purely from whether definitions changed. Together these close a state where appends kept succeeding, commands kept returning success, the observer had no failed partitions — because it was observing nothing — and the read model simply never updated (#4052)

# Summary

18.4.0 was a mistake and this withdraws it. It answered a narrow problem — an append notification that reported an occurrence time and a content hash it did not have — by returning the full stored context of every appended event through the write path, roughly 400 bytes per event, behind three new contract messages. Chronicle already has two ways to learn what was stored: read the event, or observe it. The only consumer of that notification in this repository is the integration-test collection, which asserts on sequence number and event source id.

## Changed

- An append notification reports the event as the caller asked for it, with the sequence number the kernel assigned, and claims nothing else. No invented occurrence time, no invented hash.

## Removed

- `AppendReceipt`, `AppendCausation` and `AppendIdentity`, the `IncludeReceipt`/`IncludeReceipts` request flags and the `Receipt`/`Receipts` response fields.
- `AppendResult.Receipt`, `AppendManyResult.Receipts` and the kernel plumbing behind them.
- The routing-omission tracking that existed to serve receipts. It never changed what reached the kernel, because the client's defaults already equal the kernel's, and it broke value equality on `EventForEventSourceId` along the way.

## Kept from 18.4.0

Authorization verdicts sent explicitly rather than omitted, which fixed authorized responses decoding as unauthorized in every proto3 client. The batch acknowledgment count guard. In-memory hash fidelity and MongoDB timestamp precision. The multi-target packaging fix. The central append route resolution.

Against pre-18.4.0 main, the wire contract now differs only by the authorization fix.

18.4.0 is withdrawn from the gate: its append contract is not the one major 18 carries. 18.0.0, 18.1.0, 18.2.0 and 18.3.0 are all still served. ## Changed

- A `[ProtectedDecision]` command now runs discoverable validators, including `ConceptValidator<T>` and `CommandValidator<T>`, whose only public constructor is parameterless and that Arc constructed itself. A validator with constructor dependencies is still refused before anything is resolved. A validator registered explicitly through a factory, an instance or another registration that supplies an instance Arc did not construct is resolved first, because only resolving it reveals what it supplies, and then refused: the command still fails and nothing the registration produced is used. Let convention discovery register the validator. Arc certifies only that it ran the parameterless constructor and that the rules and rule components are unchanged by reference; state changed after construction (including by a decorator that returns the original instance), property injection, `ApplyCondition`, cascade mode, nested child validators, static members and service locators are not covered and stay the developer's responsibility. See [protected-mode validator boundary](https://github.com/Cratis/Arc/blob/main/Documentation/backend/csharp/chronicle/read-models/injecting-into-commands.md#decision-reads-for-event-dependent-commands) (part of #2831)
- The refusal messages and the ARCCHR0011 validator advice now say why a validator was refused and what to do instead (part of #2831)

## Fixed

- An executable that references a project with a file-local type, such as the registration class the Cratis Fundamentals type discovery generator adds to every project, no longer fails to build with CS0234 in the generated `ProjectReferenceModules.g.cs`. The project reference modules generator now only names a type whose full name resolves to that type from the executable. (#2917)

## Fixed

- A custom field error on a command form field is now reported once instead of twice, so screen readers no longer read it twice (#2842)

## Added

- `[ProtectedDecision]` commands read the read models their decision depends on through Chronicle decision reads (`DecisionRead<T>` / `IDecisionReads`) inside the command's transaction. If another command changes what the decision read before this one commits, the commit is rejected as a concurrency violation (a validation result, HTTP 400) instead of overwriting it (#2828)
- `[Unprotected]`, `CommandDecisionMode`, command dependency safety checks, decision scenario helpers for `CommandScenario` (`UseDecisionReads`, `AppendConcurrently`), and the ARCCHR0011/ARCCHR0012 analyzers that point out decisions made outside protection (part of #2828)

## Changed

- Chronicle packages are updated from 19.13.0 to 19.23.0 and Fundamentals to 7.19.6 (part of #2828)
- Arc claims ownership of each command's Chronicle unit of work and commits it as owner. A failed command whose unit has enrolled decision reads is rolled back as owner (`RollbackAsOwner`); a failed command without decision reads, including every unmarked command, is rolled back through the public `Rollback()` exactly as before. A direct SDK `Rollback()` or `Commit()` (including an aggregate root commit) of a protected unit is refused with `ProtectedUnitOfWorkRequiresOwner` (part of #2828)
- `AddReadModels` registers Arc's command-aware `IDecisionReads` and `DecisionRead<T>` for every read model. In unmarked commands `IDecisionReads.GetDetached<T>` and `Admit<T>` behave exactly as Chronicle's reader; `IDecisionReads.Get<T>` and `DecisionRead<T>` are refused with a message pointing to `[ProtectedDecision]` (on 19.13 an enrolled read in an unmarked command already failed at commit) (part of #2828)

Protection is opt-in: unmarked commands keep their current behavior. A `[ProtectedDecision]` command refuses discoverable validators rather than supporting them (tracked in #2831); queries it performs still run their own validators, such as paging.

### Behavior changes from Chronicle 19.13 to 19.23

These come with the package update and reach applications without code changes:

- **Unique constraints honour `IgnoreCasing`.** The .NET client now sends `IgnoreCasing` when it registers a unique constraint. Before, the kernel stored every unique constraint as case-sensitive, so a constraint marked `IgnoreCasing` now rejects a value that differs only in casing (Cratis/Chronicle#4368, 19.22.0)
- **Constraint indexes are rebuilt at registration when a constraint's sequences change.** A constraint can declare the event sequences it applies to (`ForEventSequences(...)`, `ForEventLog()`, `EventSequences` on `[Unique]`). For each newly covered sequence the kernel rebuilds the index from existing events; a sequence no longer covered stops validating. See the known limits in Cratis/Chronicle#4408 (Cratis/Chronicle#4398, 19.23.0)
- **The ASP.NET Core event store falls back to the client options.** `UseCratisChronicle` now uses the client's configured event store unless a web-specific one is set (Cratis/Chronicle#4338)
- **Logging levels changed.** A reactor that loses its kernel connection (gRPC `Unavailable`) logs a Warning and reconnects instead of an Error; a cancelled stream logs at Debug (Cratis/Chronicle#4373, 19.22.0). The observer transition trace log category is now `StateMachine<ObserverState>` (Cratis/Chronicle#4289)
- **Unit-of-work lifecycle.** `ChronicleOptions.UnitOfWorkLifecyclePolicy` is added with `Compatibility` as the default, and `Dispose()` during an in-flight commit no longer rolls back or throws (Cratis/Chronicle#4258)

Validation is unchanged: the same validators run in the same order with the same member paths. Walkers are generated only where they are provably identical to reflection: the type and all its property-declaring bases are declared in source in the same compilation, none of them is partial (another generator could add properties), and no two public properties in the hierarchy share a name. Every other type, and runtime-typed values behind `object` or interfaces, keeps the reflection walk (Refs #2854)

## Changed

Arc serializes these types through resolved `JsonTypeInfo` instead of runtime-type overloads. An application that appends `JsonTypeInfoResolver.Combine(options.TypeInfoResolver, x)` to the chain now has Arc's resolver answer before `x` for types Arc or reflection knows; wrapping with `WithAddedModifier` and plain appends behave as before (Refs #2854)

## Changed

- Arc checks the caller's identity before and after each authorization policy, including policy construction, for both Arc and ASP.NET policies. A policy that changes the identity now denies the request immediately, and later policies are no longer run against the changed identity, so a later policy cannot restore an earlier change unnoticed (#2830)
- The authorization documentation and decision 0006 state what the identity check covers: claims, authentication type, name and role claim types and the actor chain. They also state what it does not cover: hidden state in custom principal types, or a change undone within a single policy (#2830)

## Changed

- ASP.NET model validation no longer builds `ValidationContext<T>` through `MakeGenericType` and `Activator.CreateInstance`, which NativeAOT and trimming cannot preserve. Command-only and query-only rules behave as before (#2853)

## Fixed

- A discoverable validator that derives from a non-generic intermediate base class no longer fails discovery with an `IndexOutOfRangeException`, and one whose intermediate base has several generic arguments is registered for its own model instead of the first argument (#2853)

## Added

- A named Arc authorization policy can opt in to being evaluated for unauthenticated callers: `AddArcAuthorizationPolicy<TPolicy>(name, evaluatesAnonymous: true)`. The policy then receives an empty, unauthenticated principal and decides whether to allow the guest. This works the same with Arc's `[Authorize]` and ASP.NET Core's `[Authorize(Policy = ...)]`, for commands, queries and observable queries. (#2761)
- `AddArcAnonymousAspNetAuthorizationPolicy(name)` gives the same opt-in to a policy registered through ASP.NET Core. It is checked at startup: the name must resolve to exactly one ASP.NET Core policy that doesn't require an authenticated user. Otherwise startup fails with `InvalidAuthorizationConfiguration`. (#2761)

## Changed

- Policies without the opt-in behave as before and still require an authenticated caller. Role requirements and authentication-scheme requirements always require an authenticated caller, even when combined with an opted-in policy. If several policies apply, a guest is only evaluated when every one of them opted in. (#2761)
- Arc's method-level authorization replaces the type-level declaration. A method with an opted-in policy is therefore reachable by guests even when its type requires a role. The authorization docs now call this out. (#2761)

## Security

- For commands and queries protected by a policy or authentication scheme, Arc checks the caller and the authorization requirements again immediately before the handler, query method or controller action runs, and denies the request if either changed after the policy verdict. (#2761)
- Missing or conflicting authorization configuration now denies the request with Unauthorized (403 at the HTTP endpoints) instead of running it or returning a server error, including when a custom command or query pipeline is registered. (#2761)

Decision 0006 records this and amends decision 0004.

## Added

- `IFallbackAuthorizationEvaluator` supplies baseline authorization requirements for commands and queries that declare none of their own. It is consulted only when neither the method nor the type has an explicit declaration, so `[AllowAnonymous]` members are no longer ambiguous with a baseline. Commands consult only the `Type` overload. MVC controller actions, including direct HTTP and WebSocket requests to controller-based queries, stay on ASP.NET Core authorization: use `AuthorizationOptions.FallbackPolicy` there (#2751)
- `ReceivedAt` on `CommandContext`, `QueryContext` and `AuthorizationPolicyContext`, plus an injectable `IOperationContextAccessor`, expose the time Arc received the operation. It is captured with `TimeProvider` at Arc's transport dispatch, before binding, or at pipeline entry for programmatic calls, and per subscribe operation for streams. It is Arc's receipt time, not network arrival. `ReceivedAt` takes part in record equality, so contexts from different receipts compare unequal (#2767)
- Query filters can set `SubscriptionScope` on the query context. Arc snapshots it after filtering and before the query runs, and gives each emission guard an independent copy, so guards can base decisions on membership that the arguments don't carry. Only state that Arc's JSON options serialize is kept, and a scope that cannot be represented is rejected with `InvalidSubscriptionScope`. The scope is always `null` for controller-based observable queries (#2768)

## Added

- Select a tenant with `ITenantScope.Begin` for commands, validation, queries, and tenant-scoped reads in background work. The selection takes precedence over request tenant resolution inside the current flow. Dispose to restore the previous tenant; disposal is idempotent, and disposing an outer scope early leaves an active inner tenant selected until it ends (#2747)
  - Custom `ITenantIdAccessor` registrations are preserved whether they are registered before or after Arc. Explicit tenant scopes require Arc's `TenantIdAccessor` as the effective accessor; resolving `ITenantScope` with a custom accessor throws `ExplicitTenantScopeRequiresArcAccessor` instead of silently selecting a tenant that downstream services cannot see.
  - Independent HTTP requests reset inherited tenant selection when they enter Arc's request pipeline, before authentication and tenant-bound resolution. On ASP.NET Core this covers all application middleware, but not middleware added by another `IStartupFilter` registered before Arc's. Observable emissions use the subscriber's tenant, not a producer's explicit tenant, on every streaming transport. Tasks and timers started inside a tenant scope keep its tenant after the scope is disposed: do not carry that captured context into unrelated work.
- Configurable access to the command and query introspection catalogs (`/.cratis/commands` and `/.cratis/queries`) through `Cratis:Arc:Introspection` (`ArcOptions.Introspection`) (#2764):
  - `Enabled` (default `true`): set to `false` to leave both routes unmapped.
  - `RequireAuthentication` (default `false`): deny anonymous callers. Arc.Core returns 401; ASP.NET Core uses the configured scheme's challenge behavior.
  - `Roles` (comma-separated, any one grants access, requires `RequireAuthentication`): deny callers without a listed role. Arc.Core returns 403; ASP.NET Core uses the configured scheme's forbid behavior.
  - `TrustForwardedIdentityHeaders` (default `false`): lets the Microsoft Identity Platform header handler authenticate protected catalog requests; enable it only behind a trusted ingress that replaces those headers.

  Defaults are unchanged: both catalogs stay mapped and anonymous. `/.cratis/identity-details/schema` is not affected. The JVM backend has no equivalent options.

## Changed

- Plain minimal API responses that return concepts change from objects such as `{"value":"..."}` to primitive values such as `"..."`, matching Arc-generated endpoints and the TypeScript proxies. To keep the object shape for a concept, register your own `JsonConverter<YourConcept>` with `ConfigureHttpJsonOptions`; it takes precedence for individual concepts, concept collections, and, when it implements property-name conversion, dictionary keys, whether registered before or after `AddCratisArc` (#2755)
- Only concept-related converters are added to ASP.NET Core's HTTP JSON options. Your converters keep precedence and the naming policy is unchanged; enums (including `long`-backed values), `DateOnly`, `TimeOnly`, `Uri`, and other non-concept types keep ASP.NET Core's defaults on plain minimal APIs (#2755)
- A concept query parameter is always supplied by the caller. If you injected a value into a query by registering a concept type in dependency injection, inject a service or accessor instead (#2757)
- Each JavaScript package's `package.json` now declares `"type": "module"`. `import` still targets `dist/esm`; `require` still targets `dist/cjs`, which has its own `"type": "commonjs"` marker. Applications do not need to change their import syntax (#2775)
- Custom single-input CommandForm fields receive the field id; put it on your input so the label is associated with it. For multi-input fields, set `groupRole` in `asCommandFormField` and label each option individually (#2661)
- Proxy generation looks for concept validators in dependencies that reference Arc Core directly or through another assembly, including validators derived from a shared validator base. It rejects multiple discoverable validators for a requested type, matching Arc's runtime discovery; unrelated validators no longer affect generation. A partial type-load failure in the generated assembly or the requested model's assembly fails generation; other dependencies contribute the types that load and produce a warning naming the dependency. Failures to load executable counterparts or to construct validators can still leave rules ungenerated (#2766)

## Fixed

- Concept-typed (`ConceptAs<T>`) query arguments, including nullable ones, are bound from the request on model-bound and controller-based queries. Previously they were resolved from the dependency injection container whenever it reported the type as a service, which could fail with HTTP 500. An explicit `[FromServices]` still resolves from the container on controllers. Missing or invalid required concept arguments on controller-based queries are rejected instead of reaching the action as `null` (#2757)
- Collection query arguments sent with GET or QUERY no longer run the query with silently changed values: an invalid element, or `null` in a collection of a non-nullable element type, fails validation with HTTP 400 instead of becoming the element's default value. Nested collections are rejected the same way, including on controller-based queries, and raw collection arguments rejected by the query pipeline report a validation failure naming the argument (#2789)
- QUERY bodies keep array element boundaries and empty string elements, so `["", "x"]` binds as two strings rather than one comma-joined value or `null` (#2789)
- Collections of `DateOnly`, `TimeOnly`, `Uri`, nullable value types, and `HashSet<T>` are bound from the request instead of being resolved from dependency injection or failing with HTTP 500. JSON node collections bind from QUERY bodies; GET rejects `JsonObject` and `JsonArray` collections with HTTP 400 because comma-delimited values cannot represent them. Generated proxies classify the same element types as arguments (#2789)
- Concepts on plain minimal APIs bind from and serialize to primitive JSON values, like Arc-generated endpoints: individual concepts, concept collections, and dictionaries keyed by concepts (#2755)
- OpenAPI describes concept values and collections as primitives and arrays, and resolves recursive dictionary and polymorphic references. A concept with your own converter keeps an unspecified schema unless you add a matching schema transformer. Enum schemas follow the effective numeric or string converter (#2755)
- Named imports from `@cratis/arc`, `@cratis/arc.react`, `@cratis/arc.react.mvvm` and `@cratis/arc.vite` resolve for TypeScript ESM (`.mts`) and CommonJS (`.cts`) consumers using `moduleResolution: Node16` or `NodeNext`, as well as Bundler consumers. Published declarations use fully specified `.js` relative imports, and each export selects declarations matching its `import` or `require` entry (#2775)
- Clicking a CommandForm field's auto-rendered label focuses its input, and the label gives the input its accessible name. Radio-group titles name the group without selecting its first option or firing a change event; untitled groups are rendered without an unnamed group role (#2661)
- `DbSet.Observe()`, `ObserveSingle()`, and `ObserveById()` support primary keys mapped as EF Core indexer properties, including shared-type entities backed by property bags. `ObserveById()` keeps filtering by a mapped public CLR `Id` when there is one and otherwise uses a single, non-shadow primary key; composite keys and shadow-only keys without a CLR `Id` are rejected when observation is set up. Entities with a shadow primary key stay observable through a mapped CLR `Id`, and query-context sorting works for mapped indexer properties (#2741)
- Validation rules from a `ConceptValidator` declared in a referenced project or package appear in the generated TypeScript proxies of commands and queries that use the concept, even when the command, concept and validator live in three different assemblies (#2766)

## Security

- Identity responses can no longer be stored by browser or intermediary caches and served to another user. `/.cratis/me`, `/.cratis/users` and `/.cratis/tenants` responses, including 401 and 403, and any response that writes the identity cookie carry `Cache-Control: no-store, private` and `Vary: Cookie` on both the ASP.NET Core and Arc.Core hosts. An existing `Vary` value, such as `Origin` from CORS, is kept. Responses a cache stored before you upgrade are not invalidated; evict cached identity responses if a cache in front of your application may have stored them (#2665)
- Protected introspection catalogs require an authenticated user even when the ASP.NET Core default authorization policy permits anonymous callers or an unauthenticated principal carries a listed role (#2764)
- A protected introspection catalog cannot be opened with forged `x-ms-client-principal` headers. On ASP.NET Core, startup fails with `InvalidIntrospectionConfiguration` when protection is enabled and the header handler, including subclasses, schemes that forward to it, or schemes on the default authorization policy, could authenticate these endpoints, unless `TrustForwardedIdentityHeaders` is set; this also applies when mapping directly with `AspNetCoreEndpointMapper`. Without the opt-in, the header handler does not authenticate protected catalog requests, including when a route group or named policy supplies its scheme, and rebuilding the principal's identity cannot bypass this. If header authentication succeeds before endpoint routing, the catalog returns 401. On the Arc.Core host the handler ignores those headers for protected catalogs unless trust is enabled (#2764)

## Deprecated

- `IEndpointMapper.MapIntrospectionEndpoints()` without options is obsolete; use the overload that takes the configured introspection options. Builds that treat warnings as errors report CS0618 (#2764)

## Added

- A model-bound command can declare `[BlockOnValidationSeverity(ValidationResultSeverity.Warning)]`, or `Information`, so that warning- or information-level validation failures reject it. The declared severity is the lowest severity that blocks. It applies to HTTP execution, validation, `Provide()` and in-process `ICommandPipeline` execution, and derived command records inherit it. (#2760)
- Generated TypeScript proxies carry the declared severity and apply the same threshold on the client. The server stays authoritative. An out-of-range declared severity fails proxy generation.

## Changed

- For a command that declares a blocking severity, the caller's `X-Allowed-Severity` (or `allowedSeverity`) can make validation stricter, never looser. A failure with `Unknown` severity also rejects such a command. Commands without the attribute behave as before. This deliberately differs from the caller opt-out for controller actions in #21; decision 0005 records why.

## Added

- `QueryScenario<TReadModel>` runs model-bound snapshot queries in-process through the same hosted pipeline as the HTTP endpoint, including argument conversion, authorization, validation, interceptors and owned query scopes. The principal comes from an `ICurrentPrincipalAccessor` registered in `Services`, as with `CommandScenario`. (#2762)
- `IQueryScenarioExtender` is a seam for extending query scenarios. `Cratis.Arc.Chronicle.Testing` uses it to seed read models and event history for Chronicle-backed queries, including other read model types the query reads.

- Query scenarios materialize lazy results that depend on scoped services before releasing the query scope, so the result stays readable after `Perform` returns.

Streaming (observable) queries are rejected with `StreamingQueryNotSupported` before the query method runs. Queries restricted to an authentication scheme fail closed in-process, because scheme selection needs a live HTTP context.

## Fixed

- Committing to an aggregate that already had events no longer fails with a concurrency violation when no one else wrote to it. Loading the aggregate left its expected position at zero, so any aggregate whose event source had a later event was rejected on every commit.
- The expected position is now captured before the aggregate's events are read, so an event appended by someone else while the aggregate is loading is still detected as a conflict at commit instead of being silently overwritten.
- For aggregates without event handlers, `IsNew` now reflects only the aggregate's own stream: events for the same event source in other streams no longer make it look existing.

## Fixed

- Generated TypeScript query, observable query and command proxies no longer contain whitespace-only lines, so they pass whitespace lint rules without editing generated files (#2705)

## Fixed

- GET queries honor paging and sorting parameters regardless of casing, so `sortBy`, `sortDirection`, `page` and `pageSize` sent by the generated TypeScript proxies are applied on both the ASP.NET Core and Arc.Core hosts; ordinary query argument matching is unchanged (#2758)

## Fixed

- ARC0013 no longer reports static members reached through a concept type, such as a `NotSet` sentinel or a static factory, in validator rules; nullable instance dereferences like `RuleFor(c => c.Name.Value)` are still reported (#2658)

## Fixed

- Model-bound queries no longer risk binding a dependency to the wrong parameter under concurrent first use. Parameters are classified once when the query is discovered and bound by position, instead of by comparing reflection metadata instances across calls (#2765)

## Fixed

- A frontend using `useIdentity`/`IdentityProvider` no longer gets stuck showing "not signed in" while the tab stays open. When a session that was active ends server-side (expiry, revoked access) an identity refresh now reloads the page instead of quietly settling into an unset identity nothing on the page could act on - the reload sends the browser through the ordinary sign-in redirect (see Cratis/AuthProxy#136) instead of leaving every command failing silently against a session that is already gone.

## Changed

- During a scenario, code that reads Arc's process-wide provider directly, such as the MongoDB and EF Core `Observe()` extensions, now sees the host's provider, or throws `ServiceProviderNotConfigured` when no host has set one, instead of using the scenario's provider. Command validation in a scenario is unaffected (#2763)

## Fixed

- `CommandScenario<TCommand>` no longer replaces Arc's process-wide service provider. A host that runs in-process specs keeps resolving services from its own provider after a scenario is disposed, and overlapping scenarios no longer interfere with each other (#2763)

## Fixed

- An `EventForEventSourceId` returned from a command now keeps its `Occurred` and `Tags` when appended, for a single wrapper, a collection or mixed collection of wrappers, and `EventsWithConcurrencyScopes`, on both the transactional and the immediate append path. Previously both values were silently dropped, so imported or backfilled events were recorded with the append time and without their per-event tags (#2570)

Runtime tags supplied through the command context, the original subject of #2570, are not part of this change.

## Added

- Register scoped, asynchronous authorization policies with `IAuthorizationPolicy` and `AddArcAuthorizationPolicy<TPolicy>()` on either Arc host (#2736).
- Use ASP.NET Core policies and authentication schemes on model-bound commands, queries, and observable subscriptions, following the [authorization contract](https://github.com/Cratis/Arc/blob/main/decisions/0004-evaluate-authorization-policies-asynchronously.md) (#2736).

## Fixed

- Observable streams retain their identity and service lifetime through in-flight emissions, including disconnects and failing cancellation or disposal callbacks.
- Authorization diagnostics now describe contradictory attributes accurately; ARC0021 is limited to authentication schemes without Arc’s ASP.NET Core integration.

## Security

- `Policy` and `AuthenticationSchemes` no longer silently fall back to authentication-only checks. Unknown, ambiguous, malformed, or unsupported requirements fail closed; applications using previously ignored settings must register valid policies and schemes before startup (#2736).
- Scheme-selected execution isolates the effective principal, tenant, and scoped services. Unsafe caller-supplied providers and identity-changing nested scheme calls are rejected rather than reusing services bound to another identity. Standalone Core does not support named authentication schemes (#2736).

## Added

- `CratisProxiesUseProxyFileSuffix` names generated TypeScript files `Name.proxy.ts` instead of `Name.ts`, so generated proxies can be told apart from hand-written TypeScript in the same folders. Imports between generated files and `index.ts` barrels follow the suffix; imports of modules you mapped yourself are left as mapped. Switching the option on or off replaces the previously generated files. Off by default.

## Added

- Analyzer `ARC0021` reports a `Policy` or `AuthenticationSchemes` on an authorization attribute of a model-bound command or read model. Arc enforces authentication and roles but evaluates neither of these, so the artifact is less protected than its attribute reads (#2736)
- `IAuthorizationAttributeEvaluator.GetAuthorizationRequirements`, so an evaluator can report every attribute it finds. It defaults to the existing single answer, so existing implementations keep working

## Changed

- Analyzer `ARC0020` now reports an ASP.NET Core authorization attribute only in a project without Arc's ASP.NET Core integration (`Cratis.Arc`), since that integration now enforces it (#2719)

## Fixed

- The authorization attribute evaluator specs could not fail: a null-conditional assertion skipped the assertion whenever the evaluator found nothing

## Security

- `[Authorize]` and `[AllowAnonymous]` from `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization` are enforced again on model-bound commands and read models when Arc is hosted on ASP.NET Core. Since v18.2.0 a model-bound artifact protected only with Microsoft's `[Authorize]` was open to every caller — over HTTP, over hub subscriptions and through direct pipeline execution — because the evaluators meant to honour it read Arc's same-named attributes instead (#2719)
- Every authorization attribute on a declaration now applies. Previously only the first one found was evaluated, so a second, stacked requirement — `[Roles("Admin")]` together with `[Authorize(Roles = "Auditor")]` — was silently dropped
- A declaration marked both `[AllowAnonymous]` and `[Authorize]`/`[Roles]` is always rejected as ambiguous. Previously it either threw or admitted anonymous callers depending on which evaluator was discovered first (#2714)

## Added

- Analyzer `ARC0019` reports `[AllowAnonymous]` declared on the same class or method as `[Authorize]` or `[Roles]`. Arc resolves that contradiction differently depending on evaluator order — rejecting the call in one order and admitting anonymous callers in the other — so the declaration now fails loudly at build time instead. Overriding a class on one query method is supported and not reported (#2714)
- Analyzer `ARC0020` reports `[Authorize]` or `[AllowAnonymous]` from `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization` on a model-bound `[Command]` or `[ReadModel]`. Arc enforces only its own `Cratis.Arc.Authorization` attributes on model-bound artifacts, so the ASP.NET Core attribute protects nothing: a command marked with it is open to every caller. Use the Arc attribute of the same name. Controller-based commands and queries are unaffected (#2719)

Both rules are warnings. A project that treats warnings as errors will fail to build where either applies — which, for ARC0020, is a command or query that is currently unprotected.

## Changed

- `Cratis.Chronicle`/`Cratis.Chronicle.AspNetCore`/`Cratis.Chronicle.Testing` bumped from `18.2.0` to `19.4.2` to pick up `[Encrypted]` and the read-model release fix it depends on; `Cratis.Fundamentals`/`Cratis.Metrics.Roslyn` bumped from `7.19.2` to `7.19.3` alongside it

## Fixed

- A read model injected into a command's `Handle()`, `Provide()`, or a `CommandValidator<T>` is now released (its `[PII]`/`[Encrypted]` properties decrypted) regardless of whether the *command* declares a `Subject`/`[Subject]`/`ICanProvideSubject` — most commands rely on Chronicle's implicit event-source-id subject fallback instead, which was never checked, so release was silently skipped for the common case independent of what the injected read model actually carried
- A namespace- or global-scoped `[Encrypted]` value (Cratis/Chronicle#4095) now reaches release correctly even on a read model that has no `Id`/`[Subject]` at all — the ordinary shape for that kind of value, since its key does not depend on a subject

## Fixed

- Prevent CommandForm from executing while custom field validation errors are present, including immediate and imperative submissions. (#2723)
- Keep validation messages and displayed submission results consistent when custom errors change or clear. (#2723)

## Summary

Three places where the quieter of two possible behaviours was also the less safe one, and where the C# implementation disagreed with the JVM one over the shared HTTP contract.

## Added

- `SortDirectionIsNotRecognized`, the validation failure raised for an unrecognized sort direction (#2715)

## Changed

- A query request reader that rejects input as invalid now surfaces as the documented `malformedRequest` validation failure rather than an exception envelope. Reader failures that are not validation failures are unchanged (#2715)
- The shared HTTP contract documents SSE connection ownership and the sort direction vocabulary as single behaviours, with the remaining narrower difference in what each implementation compares for ownership stated explicitly (#2713)

## Fixed

- `sortDirection=descending` sorted ascending. `asc`, `ascending`, `desc` and `descending` are all accepted case-insensitively now, and any other value is rejected as `malformedRequest` with 400 instead of being answered in the opposite order to the one asked for (#2715)

## Security

- SSE subscribe and unsubscribe now verify that the caller owns the connection they name. The identity that opened the stream is captured once and compared on each control request; a mismatch returns 404, exactly as an unknown connection id does, so the endpoints never confirm another caller's connection exists. Previously a caller holding another connection's id could attach a subscription whose results were written into that caller's stream, or cancel their subscriptions (#2713)

## Added

- `HttpRequestContextEndpointExtensions` on `Cratis.Arc.Http`: `SetEndpointMetadata`, `GetEndpointMetadata`, and `AllowsAnonymous()` on `IHttpRequestContext`, so an `IAuthenticationHandler` can tell whether the endpoint it is about to authenticate allows anonymous access (#2706)

## Fixed

- `AuthenticationMiddleware` now sets the matched endpoint's metadata on the request context before any `IAuthenticationHandler` runs, so a handler can check `context.AllowsAnonymous()` and return `AuthenticationResult.Anonymous` instead of rejecting - and logging a rejection for - a request the endpoint never required a credential for, such as a Kubernetes health probe (#2706)

## Added

- `IHaveKnownChanges` lets an observable collection query state which of its items changed, so the delta for an emission is the one the provider already knows rather than one rediscovered by comparison. An emitted collection is still an `IEnumerable<T>` of the read model, so existing subscribers are unaffected, and a provider that cannot know what changed continues to be served by the comparison fallback.

## Fixed

- An observable collection query backed by MongoDB no longer costs time proportional to the size of the collection every time a single document changes. The change stream already names the changed document, and the observable already decides what that meant for the observed set; that verdict is now carried on the emission instead of being discarded and then rediscovered by serializing every item of the new snapshot and the previous one.
- The comparison fallback no longer serializes every item twice on every emission. Unchanged items are the very same instances the previous snapshot held, so reference equality settles most comparisons and record value equality settles the rest; serializing is now the last resort for an item type that overrides neither.
- Removing an item from a **paged** observable query now reports the document pulled onto the page to replace it, so a client applying the delta no longer ends up one row short.

## Fixed

- Treat command responses containing neither events nor concurrency scopes as successful no-ops, including inside transactions, instead of attempting an empty append. Responses with concurrency scopes continue through the existing concurrency-validation path.
- Avoid disposed cancellation-token errors when MongoDB observable queries finish or their final subscriber disconnects.

# Summary

`CommandForm` resolved a field's property by matching the first `.member` in its value accessor's source text. A field whose accessor reads the property dynamically has no such member, so every such field resolved to the same name.

This surfaced through `Components`' `AutoCommandForm`, which builds one accessor per runtime property descriptor — every generated field compiles to `instance => instance[descriptor.name]`. All fields bound to the first match, so a date-typed field received another property's string value and the whole form unmounted on first edit with `date.getTime is not a function`.

No tracking issue exists; found while exercising a generated form against Arc 22.6.2. Happy to file one if preferred over this description.

## Added

- `fieldName` on `BaseCommandFormFieldProps`, so a field can declare the command property it binds to instead of relying on inference from the accessor.

## Fixed

- Fields whose value accessor reads a property dynamically no longer all bind to the same command property, and no longer feed one field's value to another field's component.

## Notes for review

- Inference is unchanged and remains the fallback: every existing `command => command.property` caller behaves exactly as before. The prop is additive and optional.
- `cloneElement` already overwrote `fieldName`, so a caller-supplied value was previously inert; that overwrite is now a no-op when the caller supplies one.
- `extractPopulatedValues.ts` and `ValidationMessage.tsx` keep their own copies of the same heuristic and would still mis-resolve a computed accessor. Left alone deliberately — worth a follow-up, not part of a minimal fix.
- Optional hardening not included: `getPropertyName` mis-binds silently here because the matched name is a real property, so the existing dev warning never fires. A guard rejecting a match that is not a static member access on the parameter would make this loud rather than silent.
- Requires the matching `Components` change to take effect for generated forms: Cratis/Components `fix/auto-command-form-field-binding`.

## Verification

- New spec `for_CommandFormFields/when_field_accessor_is_a_computed_property.ts`: two fields with identical computed accessor source text must bind to their own properties, and editing one must leave the other untouched. Verified to fail with the change stashed and pass with it applied.
- `commands/CommandForm` suite: 14 files, 35 tests passing. Full `Arc.React` run: 130 files, 335 tests passing.

## Summary

A batch of reported issues. Most were silent failures — things that went wrong without telling anyone. Two change runtime behavior rather than just a diagnostic and are worth reading before upgrading: collection query arguments now actually bind, and a single-instance observable query now notifies when the observed document is gone.

## Added

- `detailsType` on `<Arc>`, forwarded to the identity provider, so identity details are deserialized into their declared type instead of staying raw JSON (#2583)
- `IEnumerable<TEnum>` is supported as a model-bound query argument (#2571)
- Documentation for the `skip-generated-proxies` processor in `@cratis/eslint-plugin-arc`, which excludes generated proxies from linting without a hand-maintained path allow-list (#2613)
- Reference pages for ARCCHR0004 and ARCCHR0006 (#2633, #2632)

## Changed

- A single-instance observable query — `ObserveSingle`/`ObserveById`, on both MongoDB and EF Core — now emits `default` when no document matches: after the document is deleted, after an update moves it out of the filter, and when the initial query finds nothing. It previously held the last known value forever with no signal. Guard with `hasData` / `isReady` on the client. Note a read model with `[RemovedWith<T>]` hard-deletes its document, so "the read model was removed" is this case. (#2642)
- Direct-mode WebSocket and SSE observables forward a null emission instead of dropping it, matching what the multiplexed transport already did (#2642)

## Fixed

- Collection query arguments — `IEnumerable<int>`, `IEnumerable<SomeConcept>`, and similar — are now bound from the query string. They were classified as injected dependencies, because the DI container reports it can supply any `IEnumerable<T>`, so the query ran with an empty collection and returned an empty answer while reporting success. (#2652)
- `useIdentity(type)` deserializes with the type it is given, as its documentation already promised. Previously the type was used only to decide which argument was the default and was then discarded, so any `DateOnly`, `Guid`, `ConceptAs<T>`, or nested value on identity details was raw JSON at runtime. (#2583)
- ARCCHR0004 only flags an `[EventType]` id that repeats the type name. An id that *differs* is the supported way to rename an event record while events already in the log keep resolving; following the old advice to remove it orphaned every stored event of that type. (#2633)
- ARCCHR0006 no longer flags private helper methods that reactor dispatch would never select, and is suppressed when a `[Replay]` handler is declared for the same event type. Its message now states that `[OnceOnly]` fires once per event source, not once per event — so a handler for an event that recurs on the same source would run only for the first one. (#2632, #2615)
- The proxy generator no longer deletes hand-written `index.ts` exports that point at a sibling folder or an npm package. It only ever wrote exports for files it generated, so those lines were always hand-written; `index.ts` is a merge target, not generated output. (#2621)
- A single-instance query proxy's `defaultValue` is typed as the model rather than `{} as any`, which tripped `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` in consuming applications (#2613)
- A nullable enum query parameter no longer generates a spurious class from `Nullable<T>` alongside the enum (#2571)

## Fixed

- **`--emit-interfaces` had no MSBuild property**, which left it unusable for the thing it exists for: a package generating its own TypeScript model as part of its build cannot reach a flag only the command line accepts. `CratisProxiesEmitInterfaces` now maps to it, alongside every other option.

## Added

- **Documentation for the mode** — what it emits, when to use it, when not to, and that it removes the decorators and their import but *not* an import of a type Fundamentals genuinely provides, such as `TimeOnly`. Wired into the configuration index and table of contents.

## Changed

- **The library-mode page no longer claims abstract classes are skipped.** They are not collected directly, but a concrete type's base class is followed — so an inheritance chain arrives intact rather than with its roots missing, which is what makes the mode usable for a model with an abstract hierarchy at all. Open generic definitions and their type parameters are the things actually skipped.

---

Follow-up to #2636, which added the flag and the emission mode but stopped at the CLI. Found while trying to adopt it in Cratis/Scene, whose `Cratis.Scene.Model` is exactly the intended consumer: a deliberately dependency-free package that has been hand-maintaining its TypeScript mirror because generation was not available to it.

The targets file is packed into both `build` and `buildTransitive`, so the single edit covers direct and transitive consumers.

Verified: 51 projects build in Release with 0 errors and 0 warnings.

## Summary

Keep command decisions focused on what should happen by returning command operations. Arc executes the declared work and manages optional compensation without application-written rollback stacks, while protecting already-committed and uncertain business outcomes.

This is a backend-only addition: HTTP and TypeScript command-result contracts remain unchanged. Initial support covers flat, sequential commands; compensation is best-effort and in-process, not a durable workflow.

## Added

- `ICommandOperation` with dependency-injected `Execute()` and optional `Compensate()`, plus immutable `CommandOperations` for ordered zero-to-many work.
- Automatic failure handling, reverse-order compensation, independent cleanup cancellation, and backend recovery observations for compatible command boundaries, including Chronicle's deferred event commit.
- Compiler diagnostics and generated invocation support for operation declarations, with operations excluded from generated client responses.
- `CommandScenario` cancellation support and assertions over real operation execution and compensation.
- Dedicated usage, migration, troubleshooting, and testing guides, with runnable examples for partial failure, cancellation, and Chronicle commit rejection.
- Contextual recommendations throughout Arc's existing command, tutorial, validation, and storage guidance, preserving supported direct calls and durable reactor/workflow boundaries.

Clarify how to use Arc on its own and with Chronicle, with corrected full-stack examples and testing guidance. Add an analyzer warning for ambiguous event-source identity returns without changing command execution or event-source routing.

## Added

- Add `ARCCHR0010` for keyless commands returning a raw `Guid` alongside statically identifiable untargeted events, with an optional compiler-checked code fix when the value is intended as the event-source identity.
- Add guides showing how direct command specs complement Arc pipeline and Chronicle scenario tests.

## Changed

- Separate standalone Arc behavior from optional Chronicle integration throughout onboarding, backend, and frontend documentation.
- Use strongly typed domain examples and explain prerequisites, trade-offs, and validation boundaries.

## Fixed

- Correct documentation for authorization, validation, query transports, proxy generation, persistence, and React forms.
- Preserve familiar topics and compatibility anchors while restoring tutorial composition and navigation.
- Recognize returned typed event-source identities in either tuple position when checking for ambiguous command identities.

## Summary

Handle failed commands without exposing internal server diagnostics or giving up normal form validation. `CommandForm` now separates user-facing exception feedback from the original diagnostics available to application callbacks.

## Added

- Add `exceptionMessage` for safe, localized exception text and `exceptionDisplayComponent` with exported `ExceptionDisplayProps` to replace the exception panel independently of field-validation rendering. (#2669)

## Changed

- Show “An unexpected error occurred. Please try again.” instead of raw server exception messages by default; preserve original results and diagnostics for failure callbacks. (#2669)

## Fixed

- Honor `showErrors={false}` for both default and custom exception feedback without disabling validation or execution callbacks. (#2669)
- Display safe feedback when an exception has no diagnostic messages, and clear previous exception feedback when a subsequent result succeeds. (#2669)

## Summary

`Cratis.Chronicle`, `Cratis.Chronicle.AspNetCore` and `Cratis.Chronicle.Testing` are updated from `17.0.4` to `18.0.0`, picking up [17.0.5](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v17.0.5), [17.1.0](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v17.1.0), [17.1.1](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v17.1.1) and [18.0.0](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v18.0.0).

- Chronicle 17.1.0: Ignore no longer silently fails for Recommendations, and its icon no longer matches Perform's (cratis/chronicle#3986)
- Chronicle 17.1.0: A kernel restart no longer risks a startup-recovery storm that saturates the kernel (cratis/chronicle#3997)

## Fixed

- Arc no longer captures the type universe before generated type discovery providers register, so controller discovery, the `IArcBuilder` handed to `configureBuilder` and concept type converters see every type the binding-convention assembly walk brings in (#2666)
- The `ITypes` resolved from the container is now the same instance Arc uses during setup, built from the complete provider set (#2666)
- `IDerivedTypes` is built from that same complete universe instead of the process-wide snapshot, so polymorphic JSON and the MongoDB discriminator conventions recognize `[DerivedType]` types the assembly walk brings in, and the container resolves the same instance Arc uses (#2668)

- `CommandScenario` extenders and discoverable validators, command result assertion policies, the MongoDB builder's class maps and convention packs, and MongoDB read-model command resolution are discovered from the complete type universe instead of the process-wide snapshot (#2666)

## Summary

`Cratis.Chronicle`, `Cratis.Chronicle.AspNetCore` and `Cratis.Chronicle.Testing` are updated from `16.39.1` to `17.0.4`, picking up [16.39.2](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.39.2), [16.40.0](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.40.0), [16.41.0](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.41.0), [16.42.0](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.42.0), [16.42.1](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.42.1), [16.42.2](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.42.2), [16.43.0](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.43.0), [16.44.0](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.44.0), [16.44.1](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.44.1), [16.44.2](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.44.2), [16.45.0](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.45.0), [16.45.1](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.45.1), [16.45.2](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.45.2), [16.45.3](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v16.45.3), [17.0.1](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v17.0.1), [17.0.2](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v17.0.2), [17.0.3](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v17.0.3) and [17.0.4](https://github.com/Cratis/Chronicle/releases/tag/v17.0.4).

## Added

- Chronicle 16.40.0: `ChronicleOptions.RegistrationRetry` — registering a client's artifacts is now retried with an exponential backoff instead of failing host startup when the Kernel is busy. Five attempts by default, 2s growing to 30s, all configurable (cratis/chronicle#3869)
- Chronicle 16.40.0: Failed partition attempts carry what kind of failure they were — `Handling`, `Timeout`, `Disconnected` or `Unknown` — surfaced through the client SDK and the Workbench API (cratis/chronicle#3869)
- Chronicle 16.41.0: Behavior pattern mining across every event flowing through an event store, using a bounded streaming sketch so storage scales with distinct recurring behavior rather than event volume (cratis/chronicle#3857)
- Chronicle 16.41.0: `IPatterns.GetPatternsAt` on the .NET client — a scope plus an optional moment defaulting to now, with the day and the part of the day derived using the same rule the engine bucketed events with when it mined them. `GetPatterns` remains underneath for a context that is not a moment.
- Chronicle 16.41.0: `ToTimeBucket()` on `DateTimeOffset`, the engine's own bucketing rule, so an application asking about a moment does not have to carry a second copy of it — a copy that would drift silently, returning nothing rather than failing
- Chronicle 16.41.0: `IPatterns.GetScopes` on the .NET client and the `Patterns` gRPC service, listing the scopes that hold established patterns — what a browsing surface needs before it can offer one
- Chronicle 16.41.0: **Behavior patterns** in the Workbench: a pivot over everything established, across scope, command, initiator, day, time of day, aggregate, cause and specificity, with a confidence bar on each card
- Chronicle 16.41.0: **Pattern heatmap** in the Workbench: a day-by-time-of-day grid shaded by activity on a perceptual color scale, with a panel naming what a scope usually does at a given moment
- Chronicle 16.41.0: **Backoffice** sample generating half a year of backdated internal business activity — accounts payable, the ledger, procurement, HR and payroll — where everybody holds three or four different jobs at different points in the week, and one actor deliberately has no routine at all
- Chronicle 16.42.0: `GetUsualActions` on the .NET client and the `Patterns` gRPC service — given a situation, what is usually *done* in it, ranked by confidence and at most one answer per action (cratis/chronicle#3872)
- Chronicle 16.42.0: `FacetName.IsAction`, `FacetSet.WithoutActions()` and `BehaviorPattern.AnswersFor` — the split between the action a pattern names and the context it was taken in, which mining already relied on privately
- Chronicle 16.42.1: `PatternDetection.PersistenceInterval` setting controlling how often mined behavior patterns are persisted (default 5 seconds).
- Chronicle 16.43.0: `MapValues` on `EventTypeMigration<TUpgrade, TPrevious>` — declare which value in one generation is which value in the other, once, and Chronicle applies the map forward when upcasting and inverted when downcasting. Values the map does not mention are carried across unchanged.
- Chronicle 16.43.0: `MapValues` on the migration property builder, for a translation that applies to one direction only. A direction that declares its own transformation for a property keeps it, overriding what the value map derives.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: Time Scrubber, on both the Projections and Read Models views: step a read model instance through its history one event at a time, with the state after each event and a hover describing the event and its properties.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: Snapshots of a read model instance can be asked for per event instead of per correlation, through a new `Grouping` on the snapshot request. It defaults to grouping by correlation, so existing callers are unaffected.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: A projection can be generated as client code in TypeScript, Kotlin and Elixir alongside C#, selectable in the Workbench's generated-code panel. Languages whose client has no API for a given projection style are offered only for the styles they support.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: `ILanguageService.GetLanguagesSupporting` reports which languages can generate a given projection style.
- Chronicle 16.45.0: ASP.NET Core health check for the client connection, registered automatically by `AddCratisChronicle` under the name `chronicle` with the `chronicle` and `ready` tags. `AddChronicleHealthCheck(HealthStatus)` registers it explicitly and chooses the failure status (cratis/chronicle#3943)
- Chronicle 16.45.0: `CHR0051` reports a reducer method that declares its current read model as non-nullable (cratis/chronicle#3947)
- Chronicle 16.45.0: Documentation for the `[Index]` attribute, covering why the declaration lives on the read model and how it survives a replay (cratis/chronicle#3942)
- Chronicle 16.45.0: Documentation for the client health check (cratis/chronicle#3943)
- Chronicle 16.45.2: Documentation for addressing a nested property in a migration, and for the case that needs no property operations at all — adding or removing an *optional* property at any depth, where the target generation's schema drives both the filling and the dropping (cratis/chronicle#3949)
- Chronicle 17.0.1: gRPC wire compatibility gate that runs before anything else builds, checking the contract at HEAD against every released minor of the current major and reporting each one. A major with no declared floor is compared in full. (cratis/chronicle#3873)
- Chronicle 17.0.1: `CheckCompatibility` on the connection service, so the kernel performs the one compatibility check for every client language instead of each SDK reimplementing it. A refused connection names the client version, the protocol version and the server version.
- Chronicle 17.0.1: The canonical descriptor set now ships inside the .NET, Kotlin, TypeScript and Elixir contracts packages, so a client hands the kernel exactly what it was built against.
- Chronicle 17.0.1: `ProtocolVersion` on the contracts, and `ServerVersionInfo.ProtocolVersion` on the server.
- Chronicle 17.0.1: `AllPatterns` and `AllPatternScopes` queries, so a namespace's behavior patterns can be browsed without choosing a scope first. (cratis/chronicle#3857)
- Chronicle 17.0.1: Cross-cutting existence checks for event store, application and user: a command carrying one of those concepts is rejected when the thing it names does not exist, with no per-command wiring. A command that *creates* the entity opts its own property out.

## Changed

- `Cratis.Chronicle`, `Cratis.Chronicle.AspNetCore` and `Cratis.Chronicle.Testing` are updated to `17.0.4`
- Chronicle 16.39.2: `Cratis.Arc` updated to 22.6.0. Events appended through an Arc command now carry the command that produced them, and a command executed from another command carries the one above it.
- Chronicle 16.39.2: Every `[Command]` declares a public instance `Handle()` rather than an internal one, which is the contract Arc documents and now enforces.
- Chronicle 16.40.0: When several methods on a reactor or reducer match the same event type, the public one now wins, then the one with the richest signature. A private helper extracted from a handler can no longer take that handler's place (cratis/chronicle#3870)
- Chronicle 16.40.0: A projection catches up through a single job step walking the sequence in global order, rather than one step per event source (cratis/chronicle#3869)
- Chronicle 16.40.0: Catch-up and replay bring their job steps up after subscribing has returned, so registering a projection no longer waits for them (cratis/chronicle#3869)
- Chronicle 16.40.0: `Observers.SubscriberTimeout` is now applied to subscriber calls — it previously had no effect at all. The default is raised from 5 to 30 seconds to match the bound the transport already imposes, so nothing changes for anyone who has not set it, and `0` now means waiting indefinitely rather than falling back to five seconds (cratis/chronicle#3869)
- Chronicle 16.40.0: A partition whose last attempt timed out no longer counts toward the observer quarantine thresholds, so a congested period cannot take an otherwise healthy observer out of service (cratis/chronicle#3869)
- Chronicle 16.42.0: `GetPatternsAt` answers with commands rather than with the moment it was handed. It is built on `GetUsualActions` now, which is what its name and its documentation already promised.
- Chronicle 16.42.0: `GetPatterns` is unchanged and stays the call for the opposite question — given a situation you can describe completely, including the command, which established patterns cover it. That is the check to make before flagging an action as unusual, and it is the only one of the two answerable from a keyed candidate lookup.
- Chronicle 16.42.2: The pattern miner is a per-event-store-and-namespace grain owning the mining lifecycle — sketches, restore of established patterns, and deferred persistence — with the capture subscriber reduced to extracting features and forwarding each observed batch as a single call to its store's miner.
- Chronicle 16.43.0: An event type generation whose enum only gained members, or had members renamed, no longer registers as `EventTypeSchemaChanged`. The wider member list replaces the registered schema instead. Removing or renumbering a member is still a schema change that needs a new generation.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: The Workbench is built on `@cratis/components` 4 and imports from explicit subpaths; Workbench-local components that the library now provides have been removed.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: Projection code generation is now a seam with one generator per language. `DeclarativeCodeGenerator` and `ModelBoundCodeGenerator` moved into `Cratis.Chronicle.Projections.Engine.DeclarationLanguage.CodeGeneration.CSharp`, and `LanguageService` takes the discovered `IInstancesOf<IProjectionCodeGenerator>` rather than the two C# generators directly — code that constructs these types itself, rather than resolving them, needs updating.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: `ILanguageService.GenerateDeclarativeCode` and `GenerateModelBoundCode` take the language to generate for, defaulting to C#, so existing calls are unchanged.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: Generated C# declarative projections and model-bound records are formatted over multiple lines rather than one long line.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: The Backoffice sample correlates each generated command separately, so a generated history no longer looks like a single action.
- Chronicle 16.45.0: A client call made while the connection is down now fails instead of blocking its thread. A connect timeout surfaces as `ConnectionTimedOut`, acquiring the connect lock is bounded by the connect timeout, and a failed attempt starts a back-off during which calls fail immediately with `ConnectionUnavailable`. The watchdog still reconnects in the background, so a kernel that comes back is reachable again without restarting the client (cratis/chronicle#3948)
- Chronicle 16.45.0: A reducer method whose current read model parameter is non-nullable is now rejected at registration rather than silently excluded from dispatch. The current read model is null for the event that creates an instance, so the declaration can only ever be a mistake. Methods in a `#nullable disable` context are unaffected (cratis/chronicle#3947)
- Chronicle 16.45.0: An ASP.NET Core host no longer fails to start when the kernel is briefly unreachable; the connection failure is logged and the health check reports it until the connection comes up (cratis/chronicle#3943)
- Chronicle 16.45.2: The JSON Schema `title` is no longer part of the schema comparison that guards `EventTypeSchemaChanged`. It carries the CLR record name, so comparing it made renaming a record a breaking change despite a pinned `[EventType("...")]` identifier and an unchanged property set. It stays in the stored schema for tooling (cratis/chronicle#3926)
- Chronicle 16.45.2: An event type migration can now address a property inside a nested object — `pb.DefaultValue(m => m.Price.Description, "unspecified")` writes where it belongs, and `pb.RenamedFrom(m => m.Price.Amount, e => e.Amount)` moves a top-level value into the object it now belongs to. Registration validates such a path segment by segment and rejects one that resolves nowhere (cratis/chronicle#3949)
- Chronicle 16.45.2: A `DefaultValue` whose target the generation's schema does not declare is now rejected at registration instead of skipped. Validation still exempts a default when the target generation has no schema to resolve against (cratis/chronicle#3949)
- Chronicle 17.0.1: Every gRPC service is now derived from Arc `[Command]`/`[ReadModel]` artifacts in Core rather than hand-written, completing the migration cratis/chronicle#2908 started. `Source/Clients/Api` and `Source/Kernel/Core/Services` are gone; only `Observers` and the streaming services, whose server-to-client lifetime no command or query describes, remain hand-written.
- Chronicle 17.0.1: Patterns is served by artifacts like everything else. Its five queries — `MatchingPatterns`, `UsualActions`, `PatternsForScope`, `AllPatterns`, `AllPatternScopes` — read storage and the mining engine directly, and the contract is generated from them. (cratis/chronicle#3857)
- Chronicle 17.0.1: Query parameters that name a concept are declared as that concept rather than as `string`, so the value is validated on the way in instead of being cast inside the method. The wire is unchanged — a concept still travels as its primitive.
- Chronicle 17.0.1: The two event-sequence lookups that answered with a bare `bool` and `ulong` now answer with `EventSourceEvents` and `EventSequenceTail`. The value travels as the same primitive, one level in.
- Chronicle 17.0.1: The Workbench's surfaces are served by Arc artifacts in the kernel, with proxies generated beside the features that use them rather than into a separate `Api` folder.

## Fixed

- Chronicle 16.40.0: Adding a projection to an event store with a large event log could take the application down. Registration awaited one job-step grain being created, prepared and started per event source, exceeded its response timeout, failed host startup, and the restart re-registered into the queue it was waiting on (cratis/chronicle#3869)
- Chronicle 16.40.0: A reactor's handler was silently never invoked when the reactor also had a private helper whose first parameter was the same event type. Nothing was thrown and nothing was logged; only the missing side effects showed it (cratis/chronicle#3870)
- Chronicle 16.41.0: A constraint registered while its event sequence was already active was ignored for up to a second afterwards, so appends landing in that window bypassed it silently. The sequence now re-reads constraints on its first append after activation. This reaches any application that appends immediately after registering a constraint, not only the observer case it was found through. (cratis/chronicle#3868)
- Chronicle 16.41.0: Pattern capture subscribed only at server startup, so an event store whose clients connected afterwards mined nothing at all until the next restart. Capture now also subscribes when event types are registered. (cratis/chronicle#3867)
- Chronicle 16.41.0: `CHR0024` reported a read-model mapping written as `[property: SetFrom<T>]` as having no mapping source. Both that spelling and the bare attribute on the parameter are honored at runtime; the analyzer read only the parameter.
- Chronicle 16.41.0: The Workbench pattern scope selector showed its placeholder instead of the selected scope, while the views below it were already showing that scope's patterns.
- Chronicle 16.42.1: Bulk event ingestion no longer overwhelms pattern capture: observing only mines in memory, and the scopes an interval touched are persisted on a cadence — eliminating the subscriber timeouts, failed partitions, and retry-job storms high-rate appends previously caused.
- Chronicle 16.42.1: Behavior patterns are isolated per event store and per namespace — the same scope name in two stores, or in two tenants' namespaces, no longer counts into one sketch and contaminates both sides' persisted patterns.
- Chronicle 16.42.1: Established behavior patterns survive a server restart: a scope's persisted patterns are restored into the miner before its first event after a restart is mined, instead of being wiped in favor of whatever happened to occur first.
- Chronicle 16.42.1: A namespace added while the server is running is subscribed for pattern capture immediately, instead of only after the next restart or event type registration.
- Chronicle 16.42.1: The Backoffice sample's `generate` is genuinely re-runnable: its history marker now lands on a well-known event source so the guarding uniqueness constraint actually turns a second run away.
- Chronicle 16.42.2: `FacetSet` now round-trips System.Text.Json — its deserialization constructor previously could not bind, so any behavior pattern crossing a serialization boundary threw.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: The Time Machine found no snapshots for a read model instance whose projection is keyed by a property rather than the event source.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: A projection preview returned instances without their key, so opening one in the Time Machine had nothing to look up.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: The pivot viewer clipped tile titles, lost pinch-to-zoom on trackpads and touch devices, and could leave tiles unreachable after zooming in grouped mode.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: Selecting a read model instance did not stick, which left the Time Machine disabled; selecting an event in the sequence editor showed no details.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: A details pane no longer cramps the columns of the grid beside it.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: Disabled buttons are visibly disabled, and the projection editor's help and source buttons stay inside the editor.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: Event store cards on the landing page are clickable as a whole, with the icon and title centered.
- Chronicle 16.44.0: A projection preview shows that it is running rather than appearing to hang.
- Chronicle 16.44.1: Event details in Sequences now shows the causation entry's own properties when navigating Context → causation → properties, instead of falling back to the root event context
- Chronicle 16.44.1: Navigating into the second or later causation entry now shows that entry's properties rather than the first entry's
- Chronicle 16.44.1: The property navigation breadcrumb shows which array element was navigated through, as `[0]`
- Chronicle 16.44.2: Stopped a shutdown requested during kernel startup from crashing with an unhandled exception; it now stops gracefully and logs the shutdown (cratis/chronicle#3936)
- Chronicle 16.44.2: Fixed a `NullReferenceException` when an observer activates against an unset projection definition (cratis/chronicle#3934)
- Chronicle 16.44.2: `ReactorScenario` now surfaces what a reactor handler throws instead of swallowing the exception, so throwing reactors can be specced (cratis/chronicle#3933)
- Chronicle 16.44.2: In-memory event sequence storage now records the real identity that caused an event instead of hardcoding `Identity.System`, so in-process scenarios can assert event attribution (cratis/chronicle#3928)
- Chronicle 16.44.2: `ReadModelScenario`'s `GetInstanceById` now returns `null` for an instance that was never seeded instead of throwing (cratis/chronicle#3927)
- Chronicle 16.44.2: The client now keeps retrying artifact registration in the background after it fails on an otherwise healthy connection, instead of leaving observers disconnected indefinitely until the next reconnect (cratis/chronicle#3935)
- Chronicle 16.45.0: `[AddFrom<T>]` on a property of a `[ChildrenFrom<T>]` child no longer double-counts the event that creates the child entry. Accumulating child breakdowns produced exactly twice the value on the creating event, and every later event accumulated on top of that (cratis/chronicle#3940)
- Chronicle 16.45.0: A job left persisted as running with all of its steps already completed is now finalized instead of reported as already running. Such a job stayed wedged forever and its observer could never resubscribe, leaving reactors disconnected indefinitely (cratis/chronicle#3944)
- Chronicle 16.45.0: A read model's declared indexes are now recreated on the collection a replay fills, so they survive the swap that ends the replay instead of being absent until the sink is rebuilt (cratis/chronicle#3942)
- Chronicle 16.45.1: `[Index]` on a record's positional constructor parameter now declares an index, as the documentation says it does. Previously only `[property: Index]` worked, and the difference was invisible — nothing reported that a declaration had produced no index. (cratis/chronicle#3954)
- Chronicle 16.45.2: A migration built from a nested property expression no longer fails registration with `InvalidMigrationPropertyForEventType` naming a property that exists one level down (cratis/chronicle#3949)
- Chronicle 16.45.2: A `DefaultValue` targeting a nested property no longer writes a top-level key with a dot in its name that the target generation's schema then discards, leaving old events upcasting with the value missing and no error anywhere (cratis/chronicle#3949)
- Chronicle 16.45.3: Keyed model-bound child projections continue accepting updates after replay when an explicit event key matches the child key property. (cratis/chronicle#3922)
- Chronicle 17.0.1: `DateTimeOffset` reached the wire as an empty message, so ten fields — job creation times, user timestamps, event query date ranges — carried no value to Kotlin, TypeScript and Elixir clients. .NET was unaffected, which is why it went unseen.
- Chronicle 17.0.1: The proto generator aborted for 22 of its 23 packages while exiting 0, so most generated contracts had silently stopped regenerating and an entire `SequenceQueries` service had never been emitted at all.
- Chronicle 17.0.1: Generated proto files and the descriptor set are now deleted and rewritten on every build, so a hand-applied edit to a generated file cannot survive.
- Chronicle 17.0.1: `AppendMany` was silently dropping the caller-supplied `Occurred` timestamp for every event in the batch.
- Chronicle 17.0.1: Pattern capture re-subscribes when registering event types introduces something new. A server starting against a store no client had connected to yet captured nothing at all until the next restart. (cratis/chronicle#3857)

# Summary

The causation chain named the command that produced an event but said nothing about what that command was asked to do, so two purchase orders raised by the same command were indistinguishable on it. A command's property values are now recorded alongside its name.

Because the causation is written into the event log and the event log is immutable, a value recorded there stays there for as long as the events do. Values that must not travel that way are withheld: personal data through Chronicle's existing `[PII]` marking, and secrets through a new `[NotAudited]`. A new analyzer reports a command property whose name reads like a secret and is not marked. (#2625)

## Added

- Command property values are recorded on the causation of every event the command appends, keyed by camel-cased property name, so an event says what the command was asked to do and not only which command it was (#2625)
- `[NotAudited]` keeps a value off the causation chain — on a property, on a positional parameter, or on the command itself to exclude every property at once (#2625)
- `ARCCHR0009` reports a command property whose name reads like a secret (`Password`, `Token`, `ApiKey`, `Credential`, `Pin`, `Cvv` and the like) and which is not marked `[NotAudited]` or `[PII]` (#2625)
- `CommandCausation.PropertiesFor(Type, object)` builds the causation properties for a command instance; the existing `PropertiesFor(Type)` is unchanged (#2625)

## Changed

- Values Chronicle treats as personal data are withheld from the causation chain, honoring `[PII]` on the property, the declaring type, the positional parameter, and the concept — so a concept marked once carries the marking to every command that uses it (#2625)
- A recorded value is truncated at 1024 characters and marked where it was cut, since the causation travels on every event the command appends (#2625)

## Added

- `RuleFor(...).IgnoreConceptRules()` on the concept-flavored `RuleFor` overload, so a validator can suppress a cross-cutting `ConceptValidator<T>` for one of its own properties.

`ModelGraphValidator` runs a registered `ConceptValidator<T>` against every occurrence of that concept anywhere in a model's graph, which is the point of the mechanism. It also means a command whose own property names the entity it is *creating* cannot coexist with a "must already exist" check on that concept type: the nested validator is invoked with a fresh validation context holding only the value, so it has no way to know which command carried it, and the creating command has no way to exempt itself.

The exclusion is scoped to exactly that property on that model. A sibling of the same concept type still gets checked, and the same concept type on any other model is untouched. It is only reachable from the concept overload — `IConceptRuleBuilder<T, TValue>` — so it cannot be called on a plain primitive `RuleFor`.

Consumers with no concept validators are unaffected; nothing changes unless the method is called.

## Fixed

- `useIdentity` now hands back the details it promises. The default details were substituted only when the identity was explicitly unset, so an identity that resolved while carrying no details — `isSet` is true — passed `null` through to callers, even though the declared return type says `details` is a `TDetails`. That is exactly why call sites dereference it unguarded, and one `null` reaching one of them takes the whole page down: a signed-in user got a blank screen with a `TypeError` on the first property read after their backend restarted. The default now stands in whenever there are no details to give, without displacing real ones.

## Fixed
